title: 嘉靖二十八年江南武舉鄉試錄
text:
江南武舉鄉試錄序
維歲己酉
侍御史張公奉
命按茲南土以十月己酉檄六郡之
士及良家子諳韜畧者命有司
致禮幣聘駿及推官王子鳴臣
典試事三試之汰者什七而存
===
者三錄其姓氏而上之司馬氏
事竣駿乃以語言諭衆曰盖聞
古者男子生三日父母祿持之
桑弧蓬矢以射祝之曰願其有
事於天地四方毋徒齷齪守向
舍爲也自今觀之桑弧蓬矢之
當於郊廟朝廷之用而無
punctuated:
江南武舉鄉試錄序

維歲己酉，侍御史張公奉命按茲南土，以十月己酉檄六郡之士及良家子諳韜畧者，命有司致禮幣，聘駿及推官王子鳴臣典試事。三試之，汰者什七，而存者三。錄其姓氏而上之司馬氏。

事竣，駿乃以語言諭衆曰：「盖聞古者男子生三日，父母祿持之，桑弧蓬矢以射，祝之曰：『願其有事於天地四方，毋徒齷齪守向舍爲也。』自今觀之，桑弧蓬矢之當於郊廟朝廷之用而無
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Jiangnan Military Provincial Examination

In the jiyou year [1549], Censor Zhang, acting under imperial orders to inspect this southern region, issued a directive on the jiyou day of the tenth month summoning the gentlemen of the six prefectures and sons of respectable families versed in military strategy. He ordered the responsible officials to present ceremonial gifts and engage me, Jun, together with Prefectural Judge Wang Mingchen, to administer the examination. After three rounds of testing, seven in ten were eliminated and three remained. Their names were recorded and submitted to the military authorities.

When the proceedings were complete, I, Jun, addressed the assembled men, saying: “I have heard that in antiquity, three days after a boy was born, his parents held him [?], and arrows of mugwort were shot from a mulberry bow. They blessed him, saying: ‘May he undertake service in Heaven and Earth and the four quarters, rather than merely remain confined to petty concerns, keeping to his home [?].’ Viewed from the present day, the fitness of the mulberry bow and mugwort arrows for service at the suburban sacrifices, the ancestral temples, and the imperial court, without …

===

數出辦初塲二塲試箭合用金鼓旗號響器并

punctuated:

translation_en:
…the eastern official hall. The Nanjing Minister of War, together with the officials holding the seals of the various Nanjing Chief Military Commissions and the seal-holding official of the Nanjing Embroidered-uniform Guard, shall conduct the respective tests at the Great Drill Ground. The Censorate and the Nanjing Censorate shall each dispatch one Investigating Censor to oversee the examinations. Outside the capitals, the Provincial Administration Commissions shall conduct the tests at their local drill grounds or examination compounds. In directly administered areas and along the frontiers, the respective Regional Inspectors shall select suitably central and appropriate locations for the tests.
For the Military Provincial Examinations in the two capitals and elsewhere, tea and meals for the testing officials, the officers and soldiers performing examination duties, and the candidates answering policy questions in the final session, together with the necessary paper, writing brushes, ink, vermilion pigment, and other supplies, shall be provided as follows: in Beijing, the various military camps shall supply them according to precedent; in Nanjing, the Nanjing Ministry of War shall arrange their provision using the various public silver funds held by the ministry; elsewhere, the respective Regional Inspectors shall determine suitable quantities to be supplied by the Regional Military Commissions, Provincial Administration Commissions, prefectures, and guards.
For the gongs, drums, signal flags, and other sounding instruments needed for the archery tests in the first and second sessions, the officials supervising archery and patrolling, and the officers and soldiers conducting searches and patrols in the third session, orders shall be sent to the Three Great Training Divisions in Beijing and to the Great Drill Ground in Nanjing to assign fixed numbers. Artisans and laborers to carve and print the examination questions shall be requisitioned from the prefectural and county administrations in both capitals; elsewhere, the respective Regional Inspectors shall determine their allocation and requisition. Officials assigned to print examination papers, seal candidates’ identifying information, and perform related duties shall all be appointed according to precedent.
The first session shall test mounted archery at a prescribed distance of thirty-five paces; the second shall test archery on foot at eighty paces. text:
第一場
馬上箭
第二場
步下箭
第三場
策
論
策
===
問兵家者流神秘萬變神不可測秘難爲言約
其大要則攻守奇正四者而已奇正者攻守
之資也各一其勢而互相爲用古之人有行
之者成敗之跡可得聞歟方今胡虜苗蠻南
衝北突夷險殊形而長短異技茲欲勒石燕
然標功銅柱茂建非常之業攻耶守耶奇耶
正耶將何資而可其遂言之毋讓
問羲皇以前未聞言兵自軒轅氏涿鹿之戰說
始肇焉故其著書則曰陰符與八卦相表裏
至於畫陣圖乃五似與八卦異矣其故何歟
punctuated:
第一場：馬上箭。

第二場：步下箭。

第三場：策、論。

策

問：兵家者流，神秘萬變，神不可測，秘難爲言。約其大要，則攻守奇正四者而已。奇正者，攻守之資也，各一其勢，而互相爲用。古之人有行之者，成敗之跡可得聞歟？方今胡虜苗蠻，南衝北突，夷險殊形，而長短異技。茲欲勒石燕然，標功銅柱，茂建非常之業，攻耶？守耶？奇耶？正耶？將何資而可？其遂言之，毋讓。

問：羲皇以前，未聞言兵；自軒轅氏涿鹿之戰，說始肇焉。故其著書則曰《陰符》，與八卦相表裏。至於畫陣圖乃五，似與八卦異矣。其故何歟？
translation_en:
First session: mounted archery.

Second session: archery on foot.

Third session: policy essays and discourses.

Policy questions

Question: The military strategists are subtle and secretive, with myriad transformations: their subtlety cannot be fathomed, and their secrets are difficult to express. Reduced to their essentials, these amount to just four things: attack, defense, the unorthodox, and the orthodox. The unorthodox and the orthodox are the resources of attack and defense; each has its own strategic configuration, and they function in conjunction with one another. Among the ancients were men who put these into practice. May we hear accounts of their successes and failures? Today, the Hu enemies and the Miao barbarians charge in the south and raid in the north. Level and difficult terrain present different configurations, while strengths and weaknesses vary with military skills. If we now wish to engrave our achievements on stone at Mount Yanran and commemorate our merit on a bronze pillar, magnificently accomplishing extraordinary deeds, should we attack or defend? Employ the unorthodox or the orthodox? What resources should we draw upon to succeed? Set forth your views fully, without reticence.

Question: Before Emperor Fuxi, nothing was heard of discussing warfare. Such discourse began with Xuanyuan’s battle at Zhuolu. Thus the book he composed was called the Hidden Tallies (Yinfu), which complements the Eight Trigrams as inner and outer aspects of a whole. Yet when it comes to the battle-formation diagrams he drew, there are five [?], seemingly at variance with the Eight Trigrams. What is the reason for this?

text:
隨山刋道燔爕林木則深者可入夫以姜維之
智劒閣之險尚可乘間而襲之況區區魍魎有
足多恃乎由是言之北虜悍而地夷曠兵車是
利遏其衝而禦之必有正勝之長策南蠻狡而
地險隘步卒是用分其險而乘之必收坐困之
奇功雖曰事有機宜兵難遥度而其大勢或不
出此然竊觀今之事勢與古之兵法若有背而
馳者法曰將能而君不馭者勝重其權也今也
機宜遥制於中而文法牽縛於外疚疚焉自保
===
且不暇又安望其能臨敵應變閫閾自由以成
必勝之功哉法又曰待卒如愛子故可與之俱
死又曰處之死地而後生置之亡地而後存今
也平居而衣食不給何以作其効死之心對敵
而稹軍有禁適以道其偷生之路人懷愁怨未
戰而氣已索然矣尚望其家自爲怒人自爲戰
以赴
國家之急哉此又今日之要務廟筭之所先而非
愚生之所能與也惟
punctuated: 隨山刋道，燔爕林木，則深者可入。夫以姜維之智、劒閣之險，尚可乘間而襲之，況區區魍魎，有足多恃乎？由是言之，北虜悍而地夷曠，兵車是利，遏其衝而禦之，必有正勝之長策；南蠻狡而地險隘，步卒是用，分其險而乘之，必收坐困之奇功。雖曰事有機宜，兵難遥度，而其大勢或不出此。然竊觀今之事勢與古之兵法，若有背而馳者。法曰：「將能而君不馭者勝。」重其權也。今也，機宜遥制於中，而文法牽縛於外，疚疚焉自保且不暇，又安望其能臨敵應變，閫閾自由，以成必勝之功哉？法又曰：「待卒如愛子，故可與之俱死。」又曰：「處之死地而後生，置之亡地而後存。」今也，平居而衣食不給，何以作其効死之心？對敵而稹軍有禁，適以道其偷生之路。人懷愁怨，未戰而氣已索然矣。尚望其家自爲怒，人自爲戰，以赴國家之急哉？此又今日之要務，廟筭之所先，而非愚生之所能與也。惟
translation_en:
…following the mountains to cut roads and burning the forest trees [?], even the depths can be penetrated. Despite Jiang Wei’s intelligence and the formidable defenses of Jiange, an opening could still be exploited to launch a surprise attack. How much, then, can these petty demons have to rely upon? Viewed in this light, the northern barbarians are fierce, but their land is level and open, favoring war chariots. By blocking their avenues of attack and resisting them, there must be a sound long-term strategy for victory through orthodox operations. The southern barbarians are crafty, but their land is rugged and confined, calling for infantry. By dividing their defensive positions and exploiting the openings, one can surely achieve the extraordinary feat of wearing them down without a pitched battle. Although circumstances offer particular opportunities, and military affairs are difficult to assess from afar, their broad outlines may not extend beyond this.

Yet I humbly observe that present circumstances seem to run counter to the military principles of antiquity. The military treatise says: “He whose general is capable and whose ruler does not control him will prevail.” This emphasizes the general’s authority. Today, tactical decisions are controlled remotely from the central court, while legal and administrative rules fetter commanders in the field. Anxiously preoccupied, they scarcely have time even to protect themselves. How can we expect them to adapt to changing circumstances when confronting the enemy, exercise independent discretion within their command, and achieve certain victory?

The treatise also says: “Treat your soldiers as beloved sons, and you can face death together with them.” It also says: “Place them on deadly ground, and only then will they live; put them on ground of destruction, and only then will they survive.” Today, when clothing and food are insufficient even in ordinary times, how can we inspire their willingness to fight to the death? When confronting the enemy, restrictions on ‘steadying the army’ [?] merely open a path for them to cling to life. Every man harbors sorrow and resentment; before battle has begun, their spirit is already exhausted. Can we still expect every household spontaneously to rise in anger and every man to fight of his own accord, hastening to meet the state’s emergency? These, too, are urgent matters of the present day, which should take precedence in the court’s strategic deliberations; they are beyond the competence of this foolish student to take part in. I can only ask …

title: 嘉靖二十八年江南武舉鄉試錄
text:
執事教之
第貳問　　　　　　　　袁吉
馬上中伍箭
步下中貳箭
對御兵之道存乎法弗知法者不足以握行師之
要機用兵之術存乎變弗知變者不足以敉敵
愾之竒勲何也軌衆一志之謂法法有正有譎
行正道而王焉行譎道而伯焉在乎擇之而已
===
矣相機度時之謂變變有正有竒正矣而定經
焉竒矣而通權焉貴乎神之而已矣茍知法而
不知變非善也知變而不知法非善也知法運
於變之中而變不出於法之外善之善者也非
天下之至神其孰能與於此愚介胄士也未能
備文事焉雖然隂符秘計金匱神機亦畧得其
槩矣姑述所聞以對今夫兵者天地之義氣也
於二氣屬隂於四時屬秋於五行屬金五行非
金則木頖而不制水頖而不化五行率乖其度
punctuated:
執事教之。

第貳問　袁吉
馬上中伍箭，步下中貳箭。

對：御兵之道存乎法，弗知法者，不足以握行師之要機；用兵之術存乎變，弗知變者，不足以敉敵愾之竒勲。何也？軌衆一志之謂法。法有正有譎，行正道而王焉，行譎道而伯焉，在乎擇之而已矣。相機度時之謂變。變有正有竒，正矣而定經焉，竒矣而通權焉，貴乎神之而已矣。茍知法而不知變，非善也；知變而不知法，非善也。知法運於變之中，而變不出於法之外，善之善者也。非天下之至神，其孰能與於此？愚介胄士也，未能備文事焉。雖然，隂符秘計、金匱神機，亦畧得其槩矣。姑述所聞以對。今夫兵者，天地之義氣也。於二氣屬隂，於四時屬秋，於五行屬金。五行非金，則木頖而不制，水頖而不化，五行率乖其度。
translation_en:
…May you, honored examiners, instruct me.

Second Policy Question — Yuan Ji
Five arrows hit the target on horseback; two arrows hit the target on foot.

Response: The way to command troops lies in rules. Those who do not understand rules cannot grasp the essential workings of conducting a campaign. The art of employing troops lies in adaptation. Those who do not understand adaptation cannot achieve extraordinary merit in subduing the enemy. Why is this? Bringing the multitude into order and unifying their purpose is what is meant by rules. Rules may be upright or deceptive: following the upright way leads to true kingship; following the deceptive way leads to hegemony. It is simply a matter of choosing between them. Assessing opportunities and judging the moment is what is meant by adaptation. Adaptation involves both the regular and the extraordinary: the regular establishes constant principles, while the extraordinary allows the exercise of discretion. What matters is simply to wield these with consummate subtlety. Knowing rules without knowing adaptation is no mark of skill; knowing adaptation without knowing rules is no mark of skill either. To understand how rules operate amid adaptation, while adaptation never departs from rules, is the highest skill of all. Who but someone of supreme insight could attain this?

I am a humble man of armor and helmet, not fully accomplished in literary matters. Nevertheless, I have gained some general understanding of the secret strategies of the Hidden Talisman and the wondrous workings of the Golden Coffer. Let me relate what I have learned in response.

Now, military force is the righteous vital energy of Heaven and Earth. Among the two vital energies it belongs to yin; among the four seasons, to autumn; among the Five Phases, to metal. Without metal among the Five Phases, wood would run unruly and remain unchecked [?], and water would run unruly and fail to undergo transformation [?]; all Five Phases would depart from their proper measures.

title: 嘉靖二十八年江南武舉鄉試錄
text:
故宋子罕曰天生五財民並用之廢一不可何
能去兵惟其兵之不可去也軒轅氏以生剋爲
勝負制之爲五陣以言乎步陣則兩於前伍於
後專爲右角參爲左角偏爲前拒也以言乎車
陣則軍行右轅左追前茅慮無中權後勁也故
嘗著書謂陰符與八卦相表裏其旨涉乎深其
詞入乎幾迹雖與八卦異要之直陣屬木銳陣
屬火員陣屬土方陣屬金曲陣屬水五行之生
剋嗣續歷仲離合非即八卦之進退消息異位
===
同功者乎風后氏以命將制勝作之爲陣圖八
其陣所以定位也衡抗於外軸布於內風雲附
其四維所以備物也虎張翼以進蛇向敵而蟠
飛龍翔鳥所以致用也故嘗著握奇一卷其妙
本乎奇正相生變化不測迹雖與軒轅異要之
天衡地軸以象兩儀雲龍風虎以象水火鳥翔
以象木蛇蟠以象金土八陣之縱横錯綜歛袘
出奇非即五行之生成往來異用同體者乎是
五陣亦八卦之理也八陣亦五行之象也其
punctuated:
故宋子罕曰：「天生五財，民並用之，廢一不可，何能去兵？」惟其兵之不可去也，軒轅氏以生剋爲勝負，制之爲五陣。以言乎步陣，則兩於前，伍於後，專爲右角，參爲左角，偏爲前拒也。以言乎車陣，則軍行右轅，左追，前茅慮無，中權，後勁也。故嘗著書，謂陰符與八卦相表裏，其旨涉乎深，其詞入乎幾。迹雖與八卦異，要之直陣屬木，銳陣屬火，員陣屬土，方陣屬金，曲陣屬水。五行之生剋、嗣續歷仲、離合，非即八卦之進退消息，異位同功者乎？
風后氏以命將制勝，作之爲陣圖，八其陣，所以定位也。衡抗於外，軸布於內，風雲附其四維，所以備物也。虎張翼以進，蛇向敵而蟠，飛龍翔鳥，所以致用也。故嘗著握奇一卷，其妙本乎奇正相生，變化不測。迹雖與軒轅異，要之天衡地軸以象兩儀，雲龍風虎以象水火，鳥翔以象木，蛇蟠以象金土。八陣之縱横錯綜、歛袘出奇，非即五行之生成往來，異用同體者乎？是五陣亦八卦之理也，八陣亦五行之象也。其
translation_en:
Thus Zihan of Song said: “Heaven produces the five resources, and the people use them all. Not one can be dispensed with; how, then, can arms be abolished?” Precisely because arms could not be abolished, Xuanyuan took the cycles of generation and conquest as the basis of victory and defeat and devised five formations. In infantry formations, paired units stood at the front and groups of five at the rear; a concentrated force formed the right wing, a threefold force the left wing, and a detached force the forward defense. In chariot formations, when the army marched, chariots protected the right and pursuit forces the left; scouts bearing reed standards went ahead to guard against unforeseen dangers, command occupied the center, and strong troops brought up the rear. Thus he once wrote a book stating that the Hidden Tallies (Yinfu) and the Eight Trigrams mutually illuminate one another. Its meaning reaches into the profound, and its language penetrates the subtle. Although its outward forms differ from the Eight Trigrams, essentially the straight formation belongs to wood, the pointed formation to fire, the round formation to earth, the square formation to metal, and the curved formation to water. Are not the generation and conquest, succession and alternation [?], separation and union of the Five Phases precisely like the advance and retreat, waning and waxing of the Eight Trigrams—occupying different positions but accomplishing the same work?
Fenghou, in order to appoint commanders and secure victory, made diagrams of formations. He established eight formations to determine their positions. The transverse lines stood firm outside, the axes were arrayed within, and wind and cloud were attached to their four corners: this provided the full complement of elements. The tiger spread its wings to advance, the snake coiled facing the enemy, the dragon flew, and the bird soared: this brought them into effective action. Thus he once composed a single scroll entitled Grasping the Unorthodox (Woqi). Its marvels rest on the mutual generation of unorthodox and orthodox tactics and their unfathomable transformations. Although its outward forms differ from Xuanyuan’s, essentially the heavenly transverse lines and earthly axes represent the Two Modes, heaven and earth; cloud and dragon, wind and tiger represent water and fire; the soaring bird represents wood; and the coiled snake represents metal and earth. Are not the interwoven longitudinal and transverse dispositions of the eight formations, their contraction and extension [?], and their deployment of surprise tactics precisely like the generation, completion, coming and going of the Five Phases—differing in application but sharing one underlying substance? Thus the five formations also embody the principles of the Eight Trigrams, and the eight formations also embody the configurations of the Five Phases. Their …

title: 嘉靖二十八年江南武舉鄉試錄
text:
本於河圖洛書後世兵家者流雖運精效技層
見疊出至於百千萬變然終不能逃於五行八
卦之外者故武經七書有孫子之方員牝牡衡
直方宜車輪鳳行焉有吳起之曲直銳卦車箱
車釭鵞鸛衡焉有尉繚子司馬穰苴之兵法焉
有李靖公之左右虞候四廂而中軍居於內大
赤大黑青龍白蛇以至子午卯酉而遊卒居於
外焉以是數子而合爲武經實亦軒轅之緒餘
兵家之糟粕焉耳矣雖其九變九地等法不無
===
得於臨時制勝之策而其陰謀詭計之私甚非
帝王行一不義殺一不辜不爲者之心也然則
得其法而迥出於三代之上者不有太公乎觀
其陣圖以星宿孤虛爲天陣山川向背爲地陣
編伍彌縫爲人陣而載之韜畧者則曰必走必
懼必敗必饑必亂可克可擒可虜之十勝曰敗
地圍地死地沒地竭地艱地困地患地偶地之
九敗等篇其間不無名言格論然後世有雜其
說者六韜設爲武王問荅三畧雖援軍讖其言
punctuated:
本於河圖洛書。後世兵家者流，雖運精效技，層見疊出，至於百千萬變，然終不能逃於五行八卦之外者。故《武經七書》有孫子之方員、牝牡、衡直、方宜、車輪、鳳行焉，有吳起之曲直、銳卦、車箱、車釭、鵞鸛、衡焉，有尉繚子、司馬穰苴之兵法焉，有李靖公之左右虞候、四廂，而中軍居於內，大赤、大黑、青龍、白蛇，以至子午卯酉，而遊卒居於外焉。以是數子而合爲《武經》，實亦軒轅之緒餘，兵家之糟粕焉耳矣。雖其九變、九地等法，不無得於臨時制勝之策，而其陰謀詭計之私，甚非帝王行一不義、殺一不辜不爲者之心也。

然則得其法而迥出於三代之上者，不有太公乎？觀其陣圖，以星宿孤虛爲天陣，山川向背爲地陣，編伍彌縫爲人陣。而載之《韜畧》者，則曰必走、必懼、必敗、必饑、必亂、可克、可擒、可虜之十勝，曰敗地、圍地、死地、沒地、竭地、艱地、困地、患地、偶地之九敗等篇。其間不無名言格論，然後世有雜其說者。《六韜》設爲武王問荅，《三畧》雖援軍讖，其言
translation_en:
…are rooted in the River Chart and the Luo River Writing. Although military thinkers of later ages exercised their ingenuity and displayed their skills, producing one innovation after another and devising hundreds, thousands, and tens of thousands of variations, they ultimately could not go beyond the Five Phases and Eight Trigrams. Thus the Seven Military Classics contain Sunzi’s square and circular, female and male, transverse and longitudinal, “appropriate square” [?], chariot-wheel, and phoenix-moving formations; Wu Qi’s curved and straight, pointed and trigram [?], carriage-box, carriage-hub, goose and crane, and transverse [?] formations; and the military methods of Weiliaozi and Sima Rangju. They also contain Lord Li Jing’s left and right scouting forces and four divisions, with the central army stationed within, and the Great Red, Great Black, Azure Dragon, and White Snake formations, extending to the zi, wu, mao, and you positions, with roving troops stationed outside. The writings of these several masters were brought together as the Military Classics, yet they are really only remnants of Xuanyuan’s legacy, the dregs of military learning. Although their methods, such as the Nine Variations and Nine Grounds, offer some useful strategies for securing victory as circumstances arise, the self-serving character of their secret plots and deceptive schemes is far removed from the intentions of true emperors and kings, who would neither commit a single unrighteous act nor kill a single innocent person.

Yet was there not Taigong, who grasped these methods and stood far above the Three Dynasties? Consider his formation diagrams: he used the stellar lodges and the positions of solitude and emptiness to constitute the heavenly formation; the orientations of mountains and rivers to constitute the earthly formation; and the organization of troops into units and the closing of gaps to constitute the human formation. What is recorded in the Strategies and Plans includes chapters on the Ten Victories—those certain to flee, certain to fear, certain to be defeated, certain to hunger, certain to fall into disorder, and those who can be overcome, captured, or taken prisoner—and the Nine Defeats: grounds of defeat, encirclement, death, submergence, exhaustion, difficulty, distress, danger, and confrontation [?]. These writings contain notable sayings and sound judgments, but later generations introduced other material into his teachings. The Six Secret Teachings is framed as questions and answers involving King Wu; although the Three Strategies cites the Military Prophecies, its words…

text:
兵非詭也用之者詭之也古昔聖王之用兵也
其義一而已矣以治易亂以仁易不仁而我無
利焉是故奉天之心因地之便脩人之和靜而
龍潛動而雷行晦明而象日月喜怒而合四時
神化萬變而莫可測者莫非道之妙用而非詭
也夫天地之道有陰有陽天地之運有治有亂
如循環然莫之能已聖人者天地之心也天不
言而以治易亂之命既已屬之聖人聖人者視
天下萬物混然雜生於天地之間有若一氣而
===
分者利害相屬疾痛相關彼貪昧饕餮之徒殘
賊天下如其讐仇萬人搔動莫寧其所聖人於
是乎惻然而思勃然而起運吾道以罰無道制
吾法以飭不法天之所厭吾厭之民之所仇吾
仇之兵加其國而吊其民撫循其殘傷而易其
政百姓開門而待之淅米而儲之唯恐其不至
也故曰聖王之用兵也若櫛髮耨苗所去者寡
而所利者衆也乃若後世之君欲霸者務振其
威欲富者務廣其地構禍結怨非以爲民而徒
punctuated:
兵非詭也，用之者詭之也。古昔聖王之用兵也，其義一而已矣：以治易亂，以仁易不仁，而我無利焉。是故奉天之心，因地之便，脩人之和，靜而龍潛，動而雷行，晦明而象日月，喜怒而合四時，神化萬變而莫可測者，莫非道之妙用，而非詭也。
夫天地之道，有陰有陽；天地之運，有治有亂，如循環然，莫之能已。聖人者，天地之心也。天不言，而以治易亂之命，既已屬之聖人。聖人者，視天下萬物混然雜生於天地之間，有若一氣而分者，利害相屬，疾痛相關。彼貪昧饕餮之徒，殘賊天下如其讐仇，萬人搔動，莫寧其所。聖人於是乎惻然而思，勃然而起，運吾道以罰無道，制吾法以飭不法。天之所厭，吾厭之；民之所仇，吾仇之。兵加其國而吊其民，撫循其殘傷而易其政。百姓開門而待之，淅米而儲之，唯恐其不至也。故曰：聖王之用兵也，若櫛髮耨苗，所去者寡，而所利者衆也。
乃若後世之君，欲霸者務振其威，欲富者務廣其地，構禍結怨，非以爲民而徒
translation_en:
Warfare is not inherently deceitful; those who wage it make it so. When the sage kings of antiquity employed arms, their purpose was one alone: to replace disorder with order and inhumanity with benevolence, seeking no gain for themselves. Thus they honored Heaven’s intent, took advantage of the terrain, and cultivated harmony among people. At rest they were like a dragon lying hidden; in motion, like rolling thunder. In concealment and manifestation they patterned themselves on the sun and moon; in joy and anger they accorded with the four seasons. Their wondrous transformations, endlessly varied and unfathomable, were all subtle workings of the Way, not deceit.
The Way of Heaven and Earth comprises yin and yang; the course of Heaven and Earth encompasses order and disorder, revolving in an unceasing cycle. The sage is the heart of Heaven and Earth. Heaven does not speak, yet it has already entrusted the sage with the charge to replace disorder with order. The sage regards the myriad things under Heaven, intermingled in their existence between Heaven and Earth, as though they were differentiated forms of a single vital breath: their benefits and harms are bound together, their suffering and pain shared. Those greedy, benighted, and rapacious men ravage all under Heaven as though it were their sworn enemy. The people are thrown into turmoil, and none can rest secure in their homes. At this the sage reflects with compassion and rises with resolve: he brings his Way to bear to punish those without the Way, and establishes his laws to discipline the lawless. What Heaven abhors, he abhors; whom the people regard as enemies, he regards as enemies. He sends troops against their state while bringing comfort to its people, tends those who have been injured, and changes its government. The common people open their gates to await him and rinse rice to lay it in store for him, fearing only that he will not arrive. Hence it is said: the sage king’s use of arms is like combing hair or weeding crops; what is removed is little, while those who benefit are many.
As for rulers of later ages, those seeking hegemony strive to assert their might, and those seeking wealth strive to enlarge their territory. They foment calamity and engender enmity, acting not for the people but merely …

text:
而授殷人其柄當戰之時十日亂其上面山阪
而陳天時地勢咸諄於法然前無蹈難之賞而
後無遁北之刑白刃不畢拔而紂已就戮者法
之變而不可測也是故立綱紀定名分行仁義
布德惠崇正法塞邪隧群臣親附百姓和輯上
下一心君臣同力諸侯服其威而四方懷其德
垂拱揖讓而天下響應此以道法勝者也用兵
之上也主賢將良國富兵強約束信號令明兩
軍相當鼓錞相望未至兵交接刃而敵人奔亡
者此以事法勝者也用兵之次也察九地之利
審習五行之生尅明奇正之變察行陳解贖之
數維枹綰而鼓之白刃合流矢接輿死扶傷流
血千里暴骸盈場乃以決勝此以戰法勝者也
用兵之下也彼孫武吳起者法之下者也百戰
百勝而國胥亡身胥戮何則離人之心耗國之
氣而萃天下之大禍也或曰子之言聖王之事
廟戰之筭也為將之道柰何曰道一而已矣治
心與氣而已心欲其虛氣欲其實以宗子家相
punctuated:
而授殷人其柄。當戰之時，十日亂其上，面山阪而陳，天時地勢咸諄於法。然前無蹈難之賞，而後無遁北之刑，白刃不畢拔，而紂已就戮者，法之變而不可測也。
是故立綱紀，定名分，行仁義，布德惠，崇正法，塞邪隧，群臣親附，百姓和輯，上下一心，君臣同力，諸侯服其威，而四方懷其德，垂拱揖讓，而天下響應，此以道法勝者也，用兵之上也。主賢將良，國富兵強，約束信，號令明，兩軍相當，鼓錞相望，未至兵交接刃，而敵人奔亡者，此以事法勝者也，用兵之次也。察九地之利，審習五行之生尅，明奇正之變，察行陳解贖之數，維枹綰而鼓之，白刃合，流矢接，輿死扶傷，流血千里，暴骸盈場，乃以決勝，此以戰法勝者也，用兵之下也。彼孫武、吳起者，法之下者也。百戰百勝，而國胥亡，身胥戮，何則？離人之心，耗國之氣，而萃天下之大禍也。
或曰：「子之言，聖王之事，廟戰之筭也。為將之道柰何？」曰：「道一而已矣，治心與氣而已。心欲其虛，氣欲其實，以宗子家相
translation_en:
…and placed its handle in the hands of the people of Yin. When battle came, “ten days brought disorder above them” [?], and they arrayed their troops facing mountain slopes; the timing of Heaven and the configuration of the terrain both accorded with the methods [?]. Yet there were no rewards ahead for braving danger and no punishments behind for fleeing in defeat. Before all the blades had been drawn, Zhou had already met his death. Such are the unfathomable adaptations of these methods.
Thus, establishing guiding principles and discipline, determining distinctions of status and duty, practicing benevolence and righteousness, extending virtue and beneficence, honoring proper laws, and blocking deviant paths bring the assembled ministers into loyal attachment and the common people into harmony. High and low share one mind; ruler and ministers combine their strength. The regional lords submit to his might, and the four quarters cherish his virtue. With folded hands and ritual bows, he receives the response of all under Heaven. This is victory through the methods of the Way, the highest form of warfare. When the ruler is worthy, the generals capable, the state wealthy, and its soldiers strong; when regulations are trustworthy and commands clear; and when two armies confront one another, their drums and bronze percussion instruments within sight, yet the enemy flees before the troops engage and blades cross—this is victory through methods of practical management, the second-best form of warfare. Examining the advantages of the nine kinds of terrain, thoroughly mastering the mutual generation and conquest of the Five Phases, understanding the transformations of unorthodox and orthodox operations, and investigating the calculations of formations and “release and redemption” [?], one takes up the drumsticks [?] and beats the drums. Blades clash and flying arrows meet; the dead are carried away and the wounded supported. Blood flows for a thousand li, and exposed bones fill the field. Only then is victory decided. This is victory through methods of combat, the lowest form of warfare. Those men Sun Wu and Wu Qi practiced the lowest methods. They won every battle, yet their states both perished and they themselves were both slain. Why? Because they alienated people's hearts, depleted their states' vitality, and brought together the greatest calamities under Heaven.
Someone asked: “What you describe concerns the affairs of sage kings and calculations for victory made in the ancestral temple. What is the Way of serving as a general?” The reply was: “There is but one Way: governing the mind and vital energy. The mind should be empty; vital energy should be full. Taking the roles of lineage heir and household steward …

title: 嘉靖二十八年江南武舉鄉試錄
text:
為已任一夫不獲時予之辜四海之大三軍之
衆若游刃全牛恢恢乎運之於心而有餘地死
生利害無所顧忌者此治心之旨伊吕之志也
勿貳其志勿疑其心受命之日矢死社稷愛卒
如子千人一心治衆如寡萬人一力止如丘山
發如風雨所淩必破靡不毁沮如决積水於千
仞之隄若轉員石於萬丈之谿者此治氣之道
鷹揚之業也是故士而不以天下為度而能建
功立業與日月爭光者未之有也若夫攻圍擊
刺之法刑德奇賫之數向背險易之勢車騎卒
伍之制則兵家者流固已具載又奚足云
punctuated: 為已任，「一夫不獲，時予之辜。」四海之大，三軍之衆，若游刃全牛，恢恢乎運之於心而有餘地，死生利害無所顧忌者，此治心之旨，伊吕之志也。勿貳其志，勿疑其心，受命之日，矢死社稷；愛卒如子，千人一心；治衆如寡，萬人一力；止如丘山，發如風雨，所淩必破，靡不毁沮。如决積水於千仞之隄，若轉員石於萬丈之谿者，此治氣之道，鷹揚之業也。是故士而不以天下為度，而能建功立業，與日月爭光者，未之有也。若夫攻圍擊刺之法，刑德奇賫之數，向背險易之勢，車騎卒伍之制，則兵家者流固已具載，又奚足云？
translation_en:
…as one's own responsibility: “If even one man fails to find his proper place, this is my fault.” The vast realm within the Four Seas and the multitude of the armies are like a whole ox through which a blade moves freely: one directs them in one's mind with ample room to spare, giving no thought to life or death, advantage or harm. This is the essential purpose of governing the mind, the aspiration of Yi Yin and Lü Shang.

Do not waver in resolve or harbor doubts in your heart. On the day you receive your commission, pledge to die for the altars of soil and grain. Love your soldiers as your children, so that a thousand men share one heart; govern the many as you would the few, so that ten thousand men exert a single strength. At rest, be like hills and mountains; in action, like wind and rain. Whatever you assail must fall; nothing can avoid destruction and defeat. Be like pent-up water released from a dam a thousand fathoms high, or a round stone sent rolling into a ravine ten thousand fathoms deep. This is the way to govern vital force, the achievement of one who rises like a hawk.

Thus, there has never been a man who could establish great achievements and make his brilliance rival the sun and moon without taking all under Heaven as the measure of his ambition. As for methods of assault, siege, striking, and thrusting; calculations involving punishment, beneficence, and “qi ji” [?]; the configurations of facing toward or away and of difficult or easy terrain; and the organization of chariots, cavalry, and infantry units—the military writers have already recorded these in full. What further need is there to discuss them?

text:
威制吳魏不在於八陣圖在於
鞠躬盡瘁死而後已之言子儀
興復東京匪徒以其善用兵乃
在於不以擯斥閒廢二其志不
然談兵至孫吳備矣顛反覆詭
詐身爲天下戮將之明誡也耶
人國何利哉爾諸士選藝與能
===
行將脫橐推轂慎毋以弧矢文
字自挾尚相淬礪明公私辯義
利篤忠貞一乃心德以無負
明時遴選之典異日圖制專閫扶
成天威康正八極寧定九夷無
智名無勇功
社稷靈長終必賴之則斯舉也重
punctuated: 威制吳魏，不在於八陣圖，在於鞠躬盡瘁、死而後已之言。子儀興復東京，匪徒以其善用兵，乃在於不以擯斥閒廢二其志。不然，談兵至孫吳備矣，顛反覆詭詐，身爲天下戮，將之明誡也。耶人國何利哉？爾諸士選藝與能，行將脫橐推轂，慎毋以弧矢文字自挾，尚相淬礪，明公私，辯義利，篤忠貞，一乃心德，以無負明時遴選之典。異日圖制專閫，扶成天威，康正八極，寧定九夷，無智名，無勇功，社稷靈長終必賴之，則斯舉也重。
translation_en:
…His power to hold Wu and Wei in check lay not in the Diagram of the Eight Formations, but in his words: “Bend oneself to the task and expend every effort, ceasing only at death.” Ziyi’s restoration of the Eastern Capital depended not merely on his skill in employing troops, but on his refusal to waver in purpose when dismissed and left without employment. Otherwise, discussion of warfare had already reached completeness with Sun Wu and Wu Qi; yet perversity, vacillation, and deceit brought execution upon their practitioners at the hands of the realm—a clear warning to commanders. What benefit could this bring to a person’s state [?]?

You gentlemen have been selected for your skills and abilities, and will soon unpack your bow cases and receive military commands. Take care not to pride yourselves on archery and literary accomplishment. Rather, sharpen and temper one another; distinguish public duty from private interest, and righteousness from profit; remain steadfast in loyalty and integrity; and unite your minds and moral purpose, so as not to fail the selection instituted in this enlightened age. In days to come, when you devise military measures and exercise independent command, uphold the majesty of the throne, bring peace and order to the eight extremities, and pacify the Nine Yi. Without a reputation for cleverness or conspicuous feats of valor, you will ultimately be those upon whom the enduring vitality of the altars of soil and grain depends. Thus this examination is a matter of great consequence…

title: 嘉靖二十八年江南武舉鄉試錄
